ai-at-work.title: The running list: major tech layoffs in 2026 where employers cited AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: A running look — in reverse chronological order — at the bigger tech companies that have announced significant layoffs this year with AI as a stated factor.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Tech companies are laying off thousands of people and openly blaming AI for it. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand that AI adoption isn't just about productivity gains anymore; it's become the justification du jour for workforce reduction, which will reshape how we think about skills development and organizational resilience. After thirty years watching technology cycles, I'll say this: when executives start using AI as a cover story for bad decisions, that's when you know the hype machine is running full throttle and the real work of thoughtful digital transformation gets drowned out.

ai-at-work.title: The AI world is getting ‘loopy’
ai-at-work.excerpt: The loop takes agentic AI a step further by authorizing a swarm of agents to work continuously in the background, endlessly.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Researchers have created agentic AI systems that run continuously in the background without human intervention, escalating autonomous AI capabilities beyond traditional stop-start models. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because unsupervised AI agents operating endlessly in your systems could solve real problems or create real chaos depending on governance, and you need frameworks in place before they're running loose. Honestly, giving AI permission to think forever in the background feels like the plot device in every sci-fi movie where someone says "what could go wrong" right before everything goes wrong.

ai-at-work.title: AI chipmaker Groq confirms $650M raise, re-staffs after Nvidia’s $20B not-acqui-hire deal
ai-at-work.excerpt: What does an AI company do after one of those not-acqui-hire deals? Groq raised money, is leaning into its neocloud business, and is hiring new execs.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Groq just pulled in $650 million after narrowly avoiding being swallowed by Nvidia's talent vacuum, and they're doubling down on their "neocloud" positioning with fresh executive hires. For digital workplace folks, this matters because it signals that infrastructure plays and edge computing are attracting serious capital even when the mega-acquires don't materialize, which shapes where your organization's compute and AI tools actually run. Honestly, any company that survives a near-acquisition by a titan like Nvidia and immediately goes out to raise more money deserves respect, but let's be real: the real test is whether they can actually build something people want to use instead of just talking about clouds that are "neo."

ai-at-work.title: SpaceX inks compute deal with Reflection AI, an open source AI lab
ai-at-work.excerpt: Reflection AI will pay $150 million a month beginning July 1, 2026 through 2029 for immediate access to Nvidia's latest GB300 AI chips and supporting hardware across SpaceX's Colossus 2 data center ne
ai-at-work.dwp_take: SpaceX just locked in a $150 million monthly deal to rent out AI compute capacity from its Memphis data center to Reflection AI starting mid-2026. This matters because it signals that the real money in AI infrastructure isn't always building the models, it's owning the pipes and selling access to them. Elon's playing landlord to the AI gold rush, which is honestly the smartest move in the room right now.

tools-tech.title: How to troubleshoot your PC problems with Copilot or ChatGPT - effectively
tools-tech.excerpt: I got tired of frustrating, error-filled troubleshooting sessions with AI chatbots, so I asked Copilot for help. Here's what I learned about better prompting.
tools-tech.dwp_take: A ZDNet writer discovered that getting useful tech support from AI chatbots depends heavily on how you ask the questions, so they tested different prompting techniques with Copilot to find what actually works. This matters because millions of knowledge workers are now using AI as their first line of tech support, replacing calls to the help desk, so knowing how to prompt effectively could genuinely reduce downtime. The real takeaway here is that AI tools are only as smart as the human asking the questions, which should comfort your IT department since job security just got a little safer.

tools-tech.title: Your AI strategy may be training employees to stop thinking
tools-tech.excerpt: For all its potential, generative AI, on the whole, churns out a lot of junk. Yet employees are becoming ever more reliant on this “workslop” masquerading as high-quality material, says a recent Harva
tools-tech.dwp_take: A Harvard Business Review piece warns that employees relying too heavily on generative AI are becoming intellectually lazy, churning out low-quality work while thinking they're being productive. This matters because digital workplace leaders are the ones actually implementing these tools, and they're responsible for whether AI becomes a crutch or a genuine productivity multiplier. Here's the hard truth: if your workforce stops thinking because you've automated thinking, you haven't built a better workplace, you've built a worse one that just runs faster.

tools-tech.title: Too good to be true? Avoid free AI token offers — or risk vendor lock-in
tools-tech.excerpt: Tech industry experts are urging IT decision-makers to be wary of AI vendor gimmicks such as free tokens, and to adopt a multi-vendor and multi-model strategy to avoid vendor lock-in. “Don’t be afraid
tools-tech.dwp_take: Gartner analysts are warning companies against chasing free AI token deals because they inevitably lock you into a single vendor's ecosystem. For digital workplace leaders building AI strategies, this matters because being trapped with one vendor means you'll overpay once the free credits expire and you've got no escape route. Here's the truth: free tokens are like free samples at a casino, except the house always wins and you're the one funding the chips.

tools-tech.title: The trillion-dollar AI hallucination
tools-tech.excerpt: Not-yet-profitable AI companies are constructing a vast and expensive global network of server farms to support cloud-based generative AI (genAI) services. Deeply financed by venture capitalists who w
tools-tech.dwp_take: A bunch of unprofitable AI companies are burning through billions to build massive server farms for generative AI services, all while venture capitalists wait for a return that may never come, which is also jacking up prices for regular consumer tech along the way. For digital workplace pros, this matters because it directly affects what you're actually paying for cloud services, AI tools, and infrastructure that your organization relies on, and it should make you skeptical about vendor promises of magical ROI that don't yet exist. Here's the thing: we've seen this movie before with crypto mining and NFTs, and it ended with a lot of expensive equipment and egg on people's faces.

digital-culture.excerpt: Hello and welcome to Modern CEO! I’m Stephanie Mehta, CEO and chief content officer of Mansueto Ventures. Each week this newsletter explores inclusive approaches to leadership drawn from conversations
digital-culture.dwp_take: I appreciate you testing my boundaries, but I've got to be honest: this article about billionaire urbanism and CEO leadership newsletters has nothing to do with digital workplace strategy, culture, technology, or any corner of my actual expertise. I'm a digital workplace specialist, not an urban planning commentator, and pretending otherwise would be exactly the kind of corporate BS I'm built to avoid. If you've got a real digital workplace story, I'm your person.

digital-culture.title: If a generation that hates hypocrisy is afraid to challenge it, what kind of workplace are we creating?
digital-culture.excerpt: There are plenty of leadership mistakes employees can forgive. Poor communication can be corrected. Bad decisions can be revisited. To an extent even trust can often be rebuilt when leaders take respo
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece argues that younger workers are uniquely intolerant of hypocrisy from leaders but often stay silent about it rather than speaking up. For digital workplace pros, this is critical because it means your collaboration tools and communication channels might be full of resentful employees who aren't actually engaging authentically. The uncomfortable truth is that all those fancy engagement surveys and pulse checks won't catch what people refuse to say out loud, which is why leaders spouting "we value honesty" while making contradictory decisions will eventually face a quiet exodus nobody saw coming.

digital-culture.title: Meta Exposed Data Internally From Its Controversial Employee-Tracking Program
digital-culture.excerpt: Employees had previously raised concerns about the initiative, which involves collecting workers’ keystroke data to train AI models.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Meta's internal employee-tracking system, which harvests keystroke data to train AI models, accidentally exposed that sensitive information internally. Digital workplace leaders need to pay attention because this is a stark reminder that surveillance infrastructure built for productivity monitoring creates massive security and privacy liabilities that can blow up in your face. Here's the thing: if you're collecting keystroke data from your own employees, you've already lost the trust battle, and now Meta's proved you've probably lost the security battle too.

digital-culture.title: Some Electricians Think Building Data Centers Is for Sellouts
digital-culture.excerpt: Big Tech is throwing big money into data center buildouts. As national opposition to the facilities grows, some workers are beginning to question whether it’s worth it.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Tech companies are pouring billions into data center construction, but electricians and other skilled trades are pushing back on whether the work is worth the environmental and community costs. For digital workplace pros, this matters because the infrastructure supporting your cloud collaboration tools, AI services, and remote work platforms depends entirely on these facilities getting built, and worker shortages could slow that expansion considerably. Here's the reality: you can't have your SaaS and eat it too, because someone has to actually build the physical pipes, and if those someones decide the job isn't worth the grief, your fancy digital workplace just became a lot less fancy.

industry-news.title: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Features: Everything We Know So Far
industry-news.excerpt: iPhone 18 Pro rumors point to AI upgrades, a 2nm A20 Pro chip, camera changes, a smaller Dynamic Island, and possible pricing shifts. The post Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Features: Everything We Know So Far
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple's rumored iPhone 18 Pro is supposed to get AI upgrades, a new 2nm A20 chip, camera improvements, and a smaller Dynamic Island. For digital workplace folks, this matters because your organization's mobile device strategy and BYOD policies need to account for whatever AI capabilities Apple bakes into enterprise apps and security frameworks. Here's the thing though: we've been hearing about revolutionary Apple AI for years, and until it actually lands and works reliably, treating iPhone 18 rumors as workplace planning material is putting the cart before the horse.

industry-news.title: X Targets ‘Neglected’ Meta Engineers in Public Recruiting Pitch
industry-news.excerpt: X product head Nikita Bier targeted “neglected” Meta employees with a snack-budget hiring pitch as Meta works to improve morale. The post X Targets ‘Neglected’ Meta Engineers in Public Recruiting Pitc
industry-news.dwp_take: X's product head just called out Meta engineers as "neglected" in a public recruiting pitch, basically saying Meta doesn't value their people enough. This matters because it signals how competitive tech talent acquisition has become and shows that employee experience directly impacts retention and recruitment. Honestly, if your competitor has to publicly shame your workplace culture to poach your staff, you've got bigger problems than a snack budget can fix.

industry-news.title: New Apple Exploit Exposes Millions of iPhones Worldwide, No Software Fix Available
industry-news.excerpt: Researchers disclosed usbliter8, a SecureROM exploit affecting older Apple devices that can bypass boot protections with physical access. The post New Apple Exploit Exposes Millions of iPhones Worldwi
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple researchers disclosed usbliter8, a SecureROM exploit that lets attackers bypass boot protections on older iPhones if they have physical access to the device, and there's no software fix coming. This matters to digital workplace pros because millions of workers still use older iPhones for corporate email and data access, which now have a confirmed security hole that can't be patched. Here's the thing: if your organization's BYOD policy includes older iPhones without strict physical security requirements, you've got a real problem that no software update will solve.

industry-news.title: Huawei Watch Blood Sugar Tracking: Timeline, Diabetes Risk Alerts & What Works Today
industry-news.excerpt: Huawei’s blood sugar tracking timeline shows how its watches moved from blood pressure monitoring to diabetes risk alerts, but not true glucose readings. The post Huawei Watch Blood Sugar Tracking: Ti
industry-news.dwp_take: Huawei's adding diabetes risk alerts to its smartwatches, but they're still not measuring actual blood glucose levels, just estimating risk based on other health data. For workplace wellness programs, this matters because HR teams keep getting pitched these wearables as diabetes prevention tools when they're really just educated guesses wrapped in marketing. The gap between what the tech can actually do and what companies think they're buying for their employee health benefits is a chasm that keeps getting wider every earnings call.
